# Venue: NeurIPS 2026, Main Track

Source of every requirement below: the world's venue library (`ht-role venue neurips`, retrieved by the library 2026-11-14), which cites the NeurIPS 2026 Call for Papers, Main Track Handbook, Reviewer Guidelines, the OpenReview submission form and the official style kit. I re-fetched the call and the handbook URLs on 2026-11-26 (HTTP 200) and the NeurIPS 2027 call (HTTP 404: no newer edition exists). I read the style kit's `neurips_2026.tex`, `.sty` and `checklist.tex` myself for the layout and checklist items. Planning estimates and sample statistics are marked *estimate* and are not venue rules.

## 1. The choice (the objective lets the study pick one of ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS)

**NeurIPS 2026 Main Track, contribution type "General".** Reasons, from the three venue records:

| | NeurIPS 2026 | ICLR 2027 | ICML 2027 |
|---|---|---|---|
| main text | 9 pages incl. figures and tables, one column (5.5 in) | 9 pages, one column (5.5 in) | 8 pages, two columns |
| mandatory checklist | yes (16 items, in the PDF) | no (AI-use statement only) | no (impact + AI-disclosure statements) |
| objective's wording ("the checklist the conference requires, e.g. NeurIPS") | met by the template's `checklist.tex` | nothing to fill in | nothing to fill in |
| newest edition with a published call | 2026 (2027 call is a 404) | 2027 | 2027 |

The study is an empirical evaluation-methodology paper with many figures and a heavy reproducibility story. NeurIPS gives it the most room for figures (one column) and a checklist that asks for exactly the things the objective's rubric asks for (error bars, compute, data licences, LLM use). The outline of `story-repo` already assumes 9 pages. ICML's 8 two-column pages would cost about a page of this paper.

The NeurIPS 2026 deadline (6 May 2026) has passed; this is a simulated submission, built to the 2026 rules because that is the newest NeurIPS edition with a call. If the paper is ever submitted for real, re-check the NeurIPS 2027 call.

## 2. Hard requirements (a breach is desk rejection unless marked otherwise)

**Length**
- Main text: **at most 9 content pages, figures and tables included.** Over the limit: "will not be reviewed" (`neurips_2026.tex`, §1.1).
- Not counted: references, acknowledgments, the paper checklist, optional technical appendices. No page limit on these. (A camera-ready adds one content page; not relevant to this delivery.)
- Reviewers are not required to read the appendix: the paper must stand alone in 9 pages. Anything a claim needs goes in the main text.

**Format (the style file enforces it; do not touch it)**

- Fonts in the PDF: Type 1 or embedded TrueType only. Type 3 fonts are sent back for repair. **Matplotlib writes Type 3 by default: set `pdf.fonttype = 42`** (and `ps.fonttype = 42`) in every figure script.
- Pages are numbered (the style does it).

**Anonymity (double blind)**
- No names, institutions, acknowledgments or funding in the paper (the `ack` environment hides itself in submission mode), none in any supplementary file or linked material, none in the code. A non-anonymous URL is a violation. Own prior work: third person.

# Prior work and how the study relates to it

Only sources I consulted (abstract/listing level unless stated). Positioning is the idea's; the text is `paper-repo`'s.

## Leaderboards and their statistics
- Chiang et al. 2024, *Chatbot Arena* (ICML; arXiv 2403.04132): platform, BT fit with bootstrap CIs. We take their aggregation convention (BT-MLE, ties = half win) as the main estimator and show what the CIs do not cover.
- Zheng et al. 2023, *Judging LLM-as-a-Judge* (NeurIPS D&B; arXiv 2306.05685): MT-Bench, expert and GPT-4 pairwise judgments of the same pairs = our matched expert vs model-judge design.
- Singh et al. 2025, *The Leaderboard Illusion* (arXiv 2504.20879): practices that distort Arena (private testing, sampling). Related, orthogonal: they study data *collection* bias; we study sensitivity of the fit to altering the data given.
- Ameli et al., *A Statistical Framework for Ranking LLM-Based Chatbots* (arXiv 2412.18407): richer statistical model (ties, covariance) for Arena; a model-side alternative to our estimators.
- Chatzi et al. (NeurIPS 2024), *Prediction-Powered Ranking of Large Language Models*: rank sets with CIs combining human and LLM-judge comparisons; relates to the sampling-noise side and to the LLM-judge design.
- *Lagrangian Inference for Ranking Problems* (Operations Research, 2022; authors to be taken from the page): inference for ranks of BT items; the sampling-noise benchmark.

## Pairwise-comparison models and estimation
- Bradley & Terry 1952; Hunter 2004 (MM algorithms, AoS 32(1)); Rao & Kupper 1967 and Davidson 1970 (ties; classical, cite from the originals); Elo 1978 (*The Rating of Chessplayers*); *Modelling Competitive Sports: Bradley–Terry–Élő Models for Supervised and On-Line Learning of Paired Competition Outcomes* (arXiv 1701.08055; Elo as online BT; author list to be taken from the arXiv page).
- Negahban, Oh, Shah 2017, *Rank Centrality* (Operations Research 65(1)): spectral aggregator, alternative estimator.
- Chen, Fan, Ma, Wang 2019, *Spectral method and regularized MLE are both optimal for top-K ranking* (AoS 47(4)): statistical theory of when the top-K is identifiable from n comparisons; we use it where the SE ∝ 1/√N scaling gives k\* ∝ z√N, the basis of the SE-unit fragility used as the cross-dataset currency.

## Perturbation, influence, robustness
- Koh & Liang 2017 (ICML, arXiv 1703.04730): influence functions.
- Broderick, Giordano, Meager 2020 (arXiv 2011.14999): approximate maximum influence perturbation, "dropping a little data". Our linear search is this idea applied to a BT conclusion, verified by exact refit.
- Hampel 1974 (influence curve), Cook 1977 (distance): background, cite from originals if used.
- Min et al. 2025, *Improving Your Model Ranking on Chatbot Arena by Vote Rigging* (ICML; arXiv 2501.17858): insertion/rigging attacks. Threat model: inserted votes go through the platform's sampler, so the attacker does not choose the opponent freely; our free-choice insertion is therefore a lower bound on attacker cost, and comparison with their strategies is only under a matched (sampler-constrained) model.
- *Poisoning Attack Against Estimating From Pairwise Comparisons* (TPAMI 2021), *A Tale of HodgeRank and Spectral Method: Target Attack Against Rank Aggregation* (TPAMI 2022); *Sequential Manipulation Against Rank Aggregation* (TPAMI 2024): attacks on pairwise rank aggregation, designed per system.
- *Rank List Sensitivity of Recommender Systems to Interaction Perturbations* (CIKM 2022): sensitivity measure in recsys; analogous but not about BT/leaderboards.
- Top-K ranking with a monotone adversary (arXiv 2402.07445): theory on adversarial edge additions.

## Not read, by design or availability
- Huang et al. 2025 (arXiv 2508.11847), on the starter list: **not read** (the objective forbids the published paper on this question; this item may be it). Cite as listed in `starter_literature.md` only; reproduction notes say it was not read.

shown.message:
The paper skeleton and build command are pushed to `dev`. No results have arrived yet, so the abstract, introduction, method, experiments, discussion and appendix are still empty stubs.

- **Venue request (`paper-repo`#3):** I answered with the delivered paths and closed it. The compiled PDF will be `paper/main.pdf`, built by the system rather than committed. The LaTeX main file, the unmodified NeurIPS 2026 style file, `checklist.tex` and the bibliography are all in `paper/`. The reproduction README is `REPRODUCE.md`, and `venue-artifacts.json` is now `venue-repo`'s line in `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS`.
- **Build:** `.forgejo/document.json` runs `latexmk` in `paper/`. It builds locally; the only pages so far are the unfilled checklist.
- **Written so far:** the Related Work section and `references.bib`. I checked the authors, venues and page ranges of the cited entries against Crossref and arXiv, except Hunter 2004 and Bradley–Terry 1952, whose Crossref records I only read for volume and pages.
- **Starter item 8:** it is cited only as the starter list gives it, marked as not read. I didn't look it up.
- **Still to do:** the method and results sections wait for `experiment-repo`'s synthetic check, which decides the measure's name, and for the core results. The checklist is also unfilled.

I'll offer a `release` version once the core results exist.
